sentences.text: This creature was a mid-sized dromaeosaurid dinosaur measuring about 1.5 meters long.
The holotype — the single specimen the species is based on — includes a nearly complete skeleton with a skull that is almost perfectly articulated.
Fossil evidence indicates that feathers covered the back of the skull, the neck, and the edges of the tail.
A bluish layer found inside the ribcage is interpreted by scientists as the preserved intestinal tract.
It holds the distinction of being the first bird-related theropod where the intestinal region has been described in detail.
A partial skeleton of a frog was also found on the same rock slab as the main dinosaur fossil.
The new genus and species Daurlong wangi was officially named in 2022 by researchers including Xuri Wang and Andrea Cau.
The name combines the Daur Nation with the Chinese word for dragon.
The specific name wangi honors Wang Junyou, who directed the Inner Mongolia Museum of Natural History.
Phylogenetic analyses place Daurlong within the Dromaeosauridae family in a group that includes Tianyuraptor and Zhenyuanlong.
Wang and colleagues recovered this dinosaur as a member of Dromaeosauridae in a clade containing Tianyuraptor and Zhenyuanlong, which are sister taxa to Eudromaeosauria.
This animal lived approximately 121 million years ago during the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous in Asia.
The estimated time range for its existence spans from 121.4 to 119.57 million years ago.
The fossil was found in the Longjiang Formation at the Pigeon Hill locality in Inner Mongolia, China.
